title: Operator-led CD branching strategy and Terraform interface notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an operator-driven CD pattern for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments that blends GitOps (ArgoCD/ApplicationSet) with Terraform-managed infra contracts. Goal: make upgrades predictable, auditable, and reversible while minimizing per-customer hand-holding for image promotion and attestation.

Summary (one-pager):
- Operators push release artifacts (OCI bundles) into the shared registry and attach a signed endorsement.
- Terraform exports an immutable artifact reference (digest) and a deployment contract object (S3/TF state output or TFC variable) that downstream Argo Applications consume.
- Argo reconciles per-customer ApplicationSets using the contract; rollout phases (canary -> ramp -> full) are driven by ApplicationSet parameters and rollout hooks.
- Image attestation via cosign (sigstore) is required for any artifact promoted to the operator channel.

Key concepts / vocabulary we use here:
- Operator channel: central repo/registry + Git branch where operator-owned, signed artifacts land.
- Customer repo: per-tenant Argo/Git repo that contains values.yaml, overlay patches, and the Application manifest referencing the digest.
- Deployment contract: the minimal Terraform output used to wire infra and trigger application promotion (artifact digest, helm values bucket path, allowed-kms-key-id).

Operator CD flow (detailed):
1) Build & bundle stage (CI): produce container images and Helm chart package; create OCI bundle with chart + metadata.
   - CI creates tag 'operator-<semver>' and a digest.
   - Run unit + integration smoke tests in ephemeral environment.

2) Sign & attest:
   - cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/operator-cosign <IMAGE>@sha256:<DIGEST>
   - cosign attest --predicate attestation.json --key ksm://... <IMAGE>@sha256:<DIGEST>
   - Attestation must include: builder id, CI run id, provenance URL (github pr), SBOM link.

3) Operator promotion job (manual approval or autopromote rules):
   - On approval, operator job writes a new entry into 'operator-channel' Git branch: artifacts.yaml with digest and metadata, and updates tf-outputs bucket path.
   - Terraform module run (infra repo) consumes artifacts.yaml and writes TF output: operator_artifact_digest, operator_chart_bucket. This is the deployment contract.

4) Customer promotion (Argo consumption):
   - Argo ApplicationSet template points at customer repo and templated values for 'image.digest' pull from the operator_artifact_digest via external-secrets or Git-ops sync using a generated k8s ConfigMap created by a small sync-controller.
   - ApplicationSet rollout params: phase=canary (5%), monitor=10m, metrics=[p50-latency, error-rate, cpu].

Terraform module notes (interface recommendations):
- Module outputs (strings): operator_artifact_digest, operator_bundle_s3_path, allowed_kms_key_id, attestation_url. All outputs should be stable immutables (digest or s3 path) not tags.
- Module inputs: operator_channel_bucket, artifact_lifecycle_policy, image_policy (allowlist), cosign_key_ref.
- Keep tenant infra decoupled: avoid writing tenant repo objects directly from infra module. Instead, expose outputs and let a small operator agent reconcile.
- Use a 'promotion' resource in TF (null_resource local-exec or external data) that writes an artifacts.yaml into the operator branch; make this step gated by a manual approval variable for critical upgrades.

Helm / Argo specifics:
- Helm charts should support 'image.digest' and 'image.pullPolicy: IfNotPresent' configuration. Avoid relying on tag-only updates.
- Charts must include a 'smoke' Kubernetes Job manifest (disabled by default) that runs after install and sends status to the operator webhooks. This job should return 0 on success and 2 on degraded.
- ApplicationSet pattern: use listGenerators referencing a central ConfigMap with artifact digests per-customer. The ConfigMap is updated by the operator sync job.
- Use Argo Rollout (canary strategy) or AppRollouts integration; keep rollout config in customer overlays to give teams control. Operators provide recommended default.

Image signing & key management considerations:
- Use cosign + KMS-backed keys (Cloud KMS / HSM) for operator keys. Avoid plaintext keys in CI.
- Rotate cosign keys annually; maintain a key-rotation manifest in operator repo containing previous keys' public keys for verification of old attestations.
- Implement an attestation expiry policy: artifacts older than 90 days without re-attestation move to 'archived' state in operator-channel.
- For airgapped installs: provide an 'attestation bundle' (signed SBOM + cosign signature) that offline installers can ingest.

Upgrade & rollback plan (operator-driven):
- Stage 0: Preflight (operator checks): registry scan, image signature verification, TF plan dry-run, CRD compatibility check.
- Stage 1: Canary (subset of customers or a fraction of replicas). Monitor: latency p50/p95, 5xx rate, memory pressure. Alert thresholds: p95 latency increase >30% or error-rate >1% absolute => automatic pause and rollback.
- Stage 2: Ramp (automated percentage increases every 10m with green lights).
- Stage 3: Full promotion and archive previous digest. Maintain two last digests for quick rollback.
- Emergency rollback: operator can trigger Argo rollback by flipping ConfigMap digest back to last-known-good and triggering sync. Documented runbook with exact kubectl/argocd CLI commands.

Smoke & verification hooks:
- 'post-install-smoke' job status should be annotated on the Argo Application. If job fails, mark rollout phase 'paused'.
- Add a 'verify-hook' Lambda/pager that runs synthetic requests through customer VPC (or via relay) and reports to the operator dashboard.

Checklist for release engineer (operator):
- [ ] Build bundle and attach SBOM
- [ ] Sign image and attest with cosign
- [ ] Push artifacts.yaml and trigger TF promotion job
- [ ] Run TF plan and confirm outputs
- [ ] Kick canary phase in Argo / ApplicationSet
- [ ] Monitor for 30 minutes at canary thresholds
- [ ] Ramp and re-check signals
- [ ] Document final artifacts and create release note in releases/ folder

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require tenant owners to opt-in to operator channel or should opt-out be default? (Ops/legal tradeoffs)
- How to reconcile private airgapped installs that cannot reach cosign verification endpoints? Proposal: signed offline bundle + signing-keys import script.
- Investigate using sigstore Rekor for public transparency vs private Rekor instance for customer privacy.

Appendix: helpful commands and links
- cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/operator-cosign <IMAGE>@sha256:<DIGEST>
- example TF output usage: module.operator_artifacts.operator_artifact_digest
- argocd app rollback <app-name> --to-revision <rev>
- GitHub PR example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Jira: ENGOPS-842 (promotion pipeline enhancements)

Notes: This is a working draft. Primary target reviewers: infra-operator leads, TF module owners, SREs who manage Argo fleets. Intend to convert into a playbook with CLI snippets + a short runbook checklist in Confluence once the approval path is settled.
